blanks.note: BTN: the individual CV-PDF route on the FITI training-institute site was worked to the end. https://fiti.bt/faculty-trainers/ and https://fiti.bt/about-us/fiti-management/ were read in full and list every profile PDF the site serves; apart from the two already filed (Dasho Penjore, Damche Tenzin) there are six: Gopi.pdf, Tshering-Wangmo.pdf, Tshering-Om.pdf, Sonam-Phuntsho.pdf, Pema-Thinley.pdf and Tshering-Namgyal-Resume.pdf. All six were downloaded and their employment sections read line by line. Gopi Nepal (Director, Financial Regulation and Supervision, RMA) lists 2002-present entirely inside the Royal Monetary Authority; Tshering Wangmo (Director, Foreign Exchange and Reserve Management, RMA) lists 2002-present entirely inside the RMA. Neither has any outside employer at all. Tshering Om (BDBL), Tshering Namgyal (NPPF, earlier Bank of Bhutan, Bhutan Power Corporation, Manpower Professional Services), Pema Thinley (Royal Insurance Corporation of Bhutan) and Sonam Phuntsho (teaching, FITI) are not central bank officials, so their careers are not records for this row. Two further PDFs listed on the faculty page (Subash Rai's Profile-Resume.pdf, and three faculty with no PDF link) are FITI teaching staff, not RMA. Not tested: the RMA's own annual report board/management profiles, and the board pages of Bhutan National Bank and Druk PNB Bank.

CPV: tried the hiring-firm route rather than the Banco de Cabo Verde page. Banco Caboverdiano de Negocios Relatorio e Contas 2024 (https://bcn.cv/pt_PT/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/BCN_RC_2024_PT.pdf, 186 pp., full text extracted and searched) gives the complete Orgaos Sociais list at 31 December 2024 (pp. 11-12) - ten board members named - and a clean shareholder table (IMPAR Seguros 86.76%, Cruz Vermelha de Cabo Verde 4.44%, investidores privados 8.80%) - but it carries no biographies at all, so not one of the ten careers is stated and there is nothing to connect any of them to the central bank. Two Portuguese career-phrase searches ('exerceu funcoes' / 'ex-quadro do Banco de Cabo Verde' with administrador, banco comercial, Caixa Economica, BCA) returned only Boletim Oficial bulletins and press coverage of the CGD sale of BCA, no CV. Next, unopened: BCN's separate annual relatorio de governo societario required by BCV Aviso 7/2017, which under that Aviso should carry the directors' CVs alongside the shareholder table already in hand.

VUT: the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu's own career lists were read and every career in them is public. https://rbv.gov.vu/index.php/en/about/board-of-directors/previous-board-members lists eight former general managers and governors 1981-2012 with names, titles and years only - no biography, no employer. Press Release No. 10/2021 (Appointment of Deputy Governor) gives Noel Vari's full career: 23 years at the Bank, the last 14 as Director of the Financial Regulations Department, and names no other employer. Press Release No. 02/2014 (Recent Appointments) gives two full dated careers - Branan Karae (RBV from 1998, Director of Accounts and Customer Services 2005-2011, secondment to the IMF in Washington to October 2013) and Michael Hililan (RBV from 1989, Research and Statistics 1996-1999 and 2002-2005, IMF secondment 1999-2001, Financial Markets Department 2006-2009) - and both are RBV plus the IMF only. Not tested: the board pages of BRED Bank Vanuatu, ANZ Vanuatu and the National Bank of Vanuatu, and the sista.com.vu profile 'From the corporate world to nation building' (Sereana Moira Marum), which the search returned and I did not open.

DJI: Banque Centrale de Djibouti Rapport Annuel 2024 (https://banque-centrale.dj/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Rapport-Annuel_-V.Definitive.pdf, downloaded and fully extracted) - section 'LA GOUVERNANCE DE LA BANQUE CENTRALE', subsections 1.1 Conseil d'administration, 1.2 Direction and 1.3 Organes de controle, read in full. The board section names nobody: it says only that the Conseil is chaired by the Governor and composed of 'six administrateurs nommes par decret en raison de leurs competences'. The Direction subsection names one person, Governor M. Ahmed Osman, with no career and no dates, and records that a Directeur-Executif has been designated without naming him. No biography anywhere in the document. The Financial Afrik interview of 16 April 2025 with Governor Ahmed Osman Ali was also read: it gives his university (Universite Francois Rabelais de Tours) and calls him 'ce banquier rigoureux' but names no employer and no dates. Not reached: the board/management pages of the Djibouti commercial banks - banksalaam.com, boamerrouge.com (Bank of Africa Mer Rouge) and BCIMR - which is where I would go next.

ERI: two searches establish that no career list is published anywhere reachable. A search for the Bank of Eritrea governor, board of directors and biographies returned only Wikipedia mirrors, an investing.com central-bank stub, an OpenSanctions entity page and a CIA world-leaders list; a second search adding the Commercial Bank of Eritrea, management and board returned the same Wikipedia mirrors plus the CIA 2025 world-leaders page and unrelated Ethiopian items. The Bank of Eritrea serves no governance, board or management page of its own, and Eritrea's banks (Commercial Bank of Eritrea, Housing and Commerce Bank, Eritrean Investment and Development Bank) publish no board biographies - there is no privately owned bank publishing a board page to go to as the fallback route. Recommend reclassifying ERI as structurally closed on this row rather than leaving it as a target: there is no document to read, so no future round can convert it.

BRN, a near-miss worth recording so it is not re-chased: Baiduri Bank's own management-committee page (https://www.baiduri.com.bn/about-us/our-leadership/management-committee) publishes long careers for sixteen executives and one of them is a genuine central-bank-to-private-finance move - Mastura Mohd Shafie, Head of Group Compliance from 2025, 'previously served at Bank Negara Malaysia (the central bank), Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi UFJ, EXIM Bank, OCBC and Al-Rajhi Bank'. The central bank in that career is Malaysia's, so the record belongs to MYS and not to BRN; MYS already holds four records in have_rd.json, so it would be a duplicate and I did not file it. No executive on that page states any employment at BDCB, AMBD or the Brunei Currency and Monetary Board; the rest of the stated moves are bank-to-bank (HSBC Brunei, Citibank, Standard Chartered, UniCredit, Deutsche Bank, Societe Generale) with no central bank at either end. Also read: Baiduri's Corporate Governance Disclosure 2025 PDF, which gives the shareholding structure (Darussalam Assets 75%, Baiduri Holdings 25%) and the board committee memberships but carries no director biographies. BDCB's own trade-press appointment notice (asiaasset.com, 31 December 2024) names Rashidah Sabtu, Rokiah Badar, Noorrafidah Sulaiman and Mardini Eddie but states only their BDCB posts - no outside employer, no dates - so it is not a record either.

REFUSED at round 68, and it settles a rule: an EX OFFICIO BOARD SEAT IS NOT A CAREER MOVE. The offered record was BDCB's own announcement of 21 October 2025 naming the whole board -- the Minister of Primary Resources and Tourism as chairman, the Deputy Minister of Finance and Economy as deputy chairman, the Deputy State Mufti, two Permanent Secretaries and the Solicitor General. That is the IDENTICAL document and the identical fact as the event the map already holds for Brunei, kind 'government ministers chair and sit on the central bank's board', dated 2025-10-21. Nobody moved: each member holds the ministry post concurrently and sits by virtue of it. Government control of a board is a tie and an event, which is where the map already carries it; filing it again on the career row would double-count one fact across two rows and assert a move the source does not describe. Brunei stays absent on the revolving door and needs a real career.
